metadata.author: anadim, declarative experiment wrapper
metadata.mechanism_hypothesis: One full-prefix causal attention stage may route carry information directly, making the second attention stage redundant.
metadata.name: Single-Attention Carry Decoder
metadata.research_current_explanation: Each causal attention operation can access the complete available prefix, so the second attention stage may duplicate routing capacity while adding optimization burden.
metadata.research_evidence: The two-stage attention-only parent was eligible, but visible public evidence reported zero accuracy and therefore did not establish a benefit from its second stage.
metadata.research_next_experiment: Remove the second normalization, causal attention, and residual stage while preserving width, heads, positional encoding, tied readout, and the first attention stage.
metadata.research_expected_result: The single-stage graph should preserve eligibility with fewer parameters; equal or higher public accuracy would indicate that the removed stage was unnecessary.
metadata.research_decision_rule: Retain the single-stage design if eligibility is preserved and trusted parameter count decreases; at an exact size tie, prefer higher public accuracy.
metadata.research_previous_interpretation: The attention-only parent showed that feed-forward branches were not required for eligibility, but its zero public accuracy provided no evidence that two sequential attention stages were useful.
metadata.research_challenged_assumption: The current direction assumes that carry propagation requires two sequential causal attention transformations rather than one direct full-prefix routing operation.
metadata.research_alternative_explanation: A single causal attention stage may directly retrieve the relevant prior digit and carry context, with the second stage only increasing parameters and optimization depth.
metadata.research_discriminating_evidence: Preserved eligibility with equal or better accuracy and fewer parameters favors direct single-stage routing; lost eligibility or lower accuracy favors the two-stage carry-composition explanation.
